definition: Learning a mapping from features to a known target using labelled examples, so the model can predict the target for new cases. Classification and regression are its two main forms.
Finding structure in data that has no target column, such as groups of similar rows (clustering) or a compact summary of many columns (dimensionality reduction).
An input column the model uses to make a prediction, such as days since last order. Features must be known at the moment the prediction is made.
The column a supervised model learns to predict, such as whether a customer churned. In scikit-learn it is usually called y.
Holding back part of the labelled data, never used during training or model choice, to measure how well the final model works on unseen cases.
Any scikit-learn object that learns from data with fit. Models, scalers and encoders are all estimators, and models add predict and score.
A setting chosen before training that controls how a model learns, such as max_depth or C, as opposed to parameters the model learns during fit.
When a model learns noise in its training data, so it scores far better on training rows than on new ones. The cure is less flexibility, more data or regularisation.
A simple reference model, such as predicting the majority class or a one-line business rule, that any real model must clearly beat to be worth its cost.
The difference between an actual value and the model's prediction for it. Regression metrics such as MAE and RMSE summarise residuals.
The share of the target's variance a regression explains compared with always predicting the mean: 1 is perfect, 0 is no better than the mean, and it can be negative.
An optimisation method that repeatedly computes the slope of the loss for each parameter and moves the parameters a small step downhill, scaled by the learning rate.
Rescaling columns to comparable ranges, typically mean 0 and standard deviation 1 with StandardScaler, fitted on training data only. Needed for distance-based, gradient-trained and penalised models.
Adding a penalty on coefficient size to the loss so the model prefers simpler fits. Ridge uses squared coefficients; Lasso uses absolute values and can set some to zero.
A linear classification model that passes a weighted sum of features through the sigmoid function to output a probability between 0 and 1.
A model that predicts by asking a sequence of yes/no questions about single features, chosen to make the resulting groups as pure as possible.
An ensemble that adds shallow trees one at a time, each fitted to the errors of the trees before it, with a learning rate controlling each tree's contribution.
A table counting true negatives, false positives, false negatives and true positives. In scikit-learn, rows are the actual classes and columns the predicted ones.
Precision is the share of flagged cases that are truly positive; recall is the share of truly positive cases that get flagged. Raising one usually lowers the other.
A threshold-free measure of ranking quality: the probability that a randomly chosen positive gets a higher score than a randomly chosen negative. 0.5 is random, 1.0 perfect.
The probability cut-off above which a classifier labels a case positive. The default is 0.5, but it should be chosen from the costs of each kind of mistake.
Splitting the training data into k folds and training k models, each validated on a different fold, to get a steadier performance estimate and a sense of its spread.
A scikit-learn object that chains preprocessing steps and a final model into one estimator, so every step is fitted on training data only and applied identically later.
Turning a categorical column into one 0/1 column per category so models can use it. OneHotEncoder with handle_unknown set to ignore copes with unseen categories.
Information available during training or evaluation that will not be available at prediction time, such as features recorded after the prediction date or preprocessing fitted on validation rows.
A clustering algorithm that alternates between assigning each point to its nearest centre and moving each centre to the mean of its points, for a chosen number of clusters k.
A technique that finds new axes, each a weighted mix of the original columns, ordered by how much of the data's variance they capture, so a few can summarise many.
One complete pass of a neural network's training algorithm over the whole training set. Training usually runs for many epochs while the loss falls.
A fixed-length vector produced by a model to represent a text or other item, arranged so that items with similar meaning have nearby vectors.
A change over time in the distribution of a model's inputs compared with its training data, which can make predictions less reliable and should be monitored.
